$schema-note: NS host -> DNS provider registry, maintained via pull requests. Matching: case-insensitive fnmatch-style wildcards against each NS host (trailing dot stripped). Entries are checked in file order; the first entry with a matching pattern wins. 'driver' is optional and must be one of the plugin's hardcoded drivers; entries without it render as detected-but-unsupported.

providers.name: Cloudflare
providers.source: https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/nameservers/nameserver-options/ (standard: <name>.ns.cloudflare.com); https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/foundation-dns/advanced-nameservers/ (advanced: <color>.foundationdns.{com,net,org})

providers.name: IONOS
providers.source: https://www.ionos.com/help/domains/general-information-about-dns-settings/default-dns-settings-for-11-ionos-domains/ (nsXXXX.ui-dns.{com,org,de,biz})

providers.name: Dinahosting
providers.source: https://dinahosting.com/ayuda/cuales-son-los-dns-de-dinahosting/ (ns.dinahosting.com, ns2-ns4.dinahosting.com)

providers.name: AWS Route 53
providers.source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/APIReference/API_GetHostedZone.html (delegation sets are 4 servers ns-<n>.awsdns-<nn>.{com,net,org,co.uk}, e.g. ns-2048.awsdns-64.com)

providers.name: Google Cloud DNS
providers.source: https://cloud.google.com/dns/docs/update-name-servers (ns-cloud-<shard><1-4>.googledomains.com, e.g. ns-cloud-a1.googledomains.com; keep the ns-cloud- prefix — ns1-ns4.googledomains.com is legacy Google Domains, not Cloud DNS)

providers.name: Azure DNS
providers.source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/dns/dns-delegate-domain-azure-dns (zones get ns1-<nn>.azure-dns.com, ns2-<nn>.azure-dns.net, ns3-<nn>.azure-dns.org, ns4-<nn>.azure-dns.info)

providers.name: GoDaddy
providers.source: https://www.godaddy.com/resources/skills/how-to-check-dns-and-diagnose-common-issues (GoDaddy nameservers use domaincontrol.com; assigned in pairs ns<odd>/ns<even>.domaincontrol.com — no exhaustive official list published)

providers.name: OVHcloud
providers.source: https://docs.ovhcloud.com/en/guides/web-cloud/domains/dns-server-edit (paired ns<nn>/dns<nn>.ovh.net, .ovh.ca for Canada, ns200/dns200.anycast.me for Anycast); https://docs.ovhcloud.com/en/guides/web-cloud/domains/dns-ips-update (full dns1-dns113/ns1-ns113.ovh.net list incl. legacy digitless ns/dns.ovh.net)

providers.name: DigitalOcean
providers.source: https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/networking/dns/getting-started/dns-registrars/ (exactly ns1/ns2/ns3.digitalocean.com)

providers.name: Linode (Akamai)
providers.source: https://techdocs.akamai.com/cloud-computing/docs/configure-your-domains-authoritative-name-servers (exactly ns1-ns5.linode.com, auto-created and immutable)

providers.name: Vercel
providers.source: https://vercel.com/docs/domains/working-with-nameservers (exactly ns1/ns2.vercel-dns.com)

providers.name: Gandi
providers.source: https://docs.gandi.net/en/domain_names/advanced_users/vanity_nameservers.html (Gandi LiveDNS default nameservers follow the pattern ns-<number>-<letter>.gandi.net, e.g. ns-6-a.gandi.net, per Gandi's own docs)

providers.name: Namecheap
providers.source: https://www.namecheap.com/support/knowledgebase/article.aspx/767/10/how-to-change-dns-for-a-domain/ (BasicDNS default: dns1/dns2.registrar-servers.com); https://www.namecheap.com/support/knowledgebase/article.aspx/203/32/nameserver-setup-for-shared-packages/ (shared hosting plans: dns1/dns2.namecheaphosting.com)

providers.name: Hetzner
providers.source: https://docs.hetzner.com/dns-console/dns/general/authoritative-name-servers/ (DNS Console: hydrogen/oxygen.ns.hetzner.com + helium.ns.hetzner.de; Robot secondary DNS: ns1.first-ns.de, robotns2.second-ns.de, robotns3.second-ns.com)

providers.name: Squarespace
providers.source: https://support.squarespace.com/hc/en-us/articles/4404183898125-Making-changes-to-nameservers (official: Squarespace default nameservers may end in squarespacedns.com or systemdns.com; the same page also lists googledomains.com and nsone.net as possible endings, deliberately excluded here since those domains are already claimed by Google Cloud DNS / NS1 entries in this registry and would cause first-match collisions)

providers.name: Wix
providers.source: https://support.wix.com/en/article/connecting-a-domain-to-the-wix-name-servers (Wix nameservers are account-specific and shown on-screen per domain, not published as a fixed list; observed examples across Wix's own help articles span ns1/ns2/ns5/ns6/ns14/ns15.wixdns.net, hence the open-ended ns*.wixdns.net wildcard rather than a narrow numeric range)

providers.name: Hostinger
providers.source: https://www.hostinger.com/support/how-to-fix-dns-issue-at-hostinger/ (official: Hostinger-managed domains point to nameservers such as ns1.dns-parking.com; exact enumerable set not published, so the domain-wide wildcard is used)

providers.name: Porkbun
providers.source: https://kb.porkbun.com/article/63-how-to-switch-to-porkbuns-nameservers (exactly these 4 fixed default nameservers)

providers.name: cdmon
providers.source: https://helpdesk.cdmon.com/portal/es/kb/articles/qu%C3%A9-es-el-servidor-dns-est%C3%A1tico-y-c%C3%B3mo-podemos-modificarlo (cdmon's own DNS servers: ns1-ns3.cdmon.net, ns4.cdmondns-01.org, ns5.cdmondns-01.com — note mixed TLDs, not all .com)

providers.name: one.com
providers.source: https://help.one.com/hc/en-us/articles/360000841638-How-do-I-change-the-name-servers (official: web hosting default nameservers are ns01.one.com / ns02.one.com — zero-padded form, confirmed via one.com's own support article)

providers.name: NS1 (IBM NS1 Connect)
providers.source: https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/ns1-connect?topic=nameservers-nameserver-assignments (zones are assigned dns1-dns4.p<NN>.nsone.net from a numbered pool, e.g. dns1.p03.nsone.net; NS1 was acquired by and is now documented under IBM)

providers.name: bunny.net (Bunny DNS)
providers.source: https://docs.bunny.net/dns/nameservers (standard Bunny DNS nameservers: kiki.bunny.net, coco.bunny.net; a custom-nameserver option also exists but has no fixed enumerable hostnames, so it is not covered here). Detection-only: bunny.net is a CDN/DNS host, not a domain registrar, so no 'driver' is set.
